compiled_state.title: pr-comment-response.sh fails to parse gh api --paginate output
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Reproducer
```
$ bash plugins/dso/scripts/pr-comment-response.sh --pr-number 237 --output /tmp/out.json
# returns Comments: 0  Skipped: 0 (incorrect — PR has 30 comments)
```

## Root cause
`_fetch_comments` calls `gh api ... --paginate` and concatenates pages. For PRs with multiple pages of comments, gh api's paginated output contains embedded control characters / page boundaries that break JSON parsing in `_normalize_comments`:
```
json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Invalid control character at: line 1 column 216 (char 215)
```

The script silently swallows the parse error and returns an empty comments array, so callers (including /dso:respond-to-pr-comments) get `Comments: 0` and assume the PR has no unresolved comments.

## Impact
- /dso:respond-to-pr-comments is broken on any PR with >1 page of comments
- Defenses cannot be posted via the canonical pipeline → orchestrator must fall back to raw `gh api` calls

## Discovered
While clearing llm-review block on PR #237 (the SDET audit implementation PR) on 2026-05-19. PR had 30 inline comments; script reported 0.

## Suggested fix
Stop using `--paginate` (it concatenates page bodies without proper JSON merging) and instead loop manually over pages, appending to a Python list. Alternatively, use `gh api --paginate --jq '.'` which normalizes to a single JSON array.

## Repro steps
1. Find any PR with >30 review comments on this repo.
2. Run `bash plugins/dso/scripts/pr-comment-response.sh --pr-number <N> --output /tmp/x.json`.
3. Observe: `Comments: 0` despite real comments existing.
4. Run `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/<N>/comments --paginate | python3 -c 'import json,sys; json.load(sys.stdin)'` — JSONDecodeError.
